bull_bear.body: Interim dividend of INR 15/share declared; INR 325 Cr cash balance available; Final dividend decision pending in Sept 2026; Buyback under evaluation but constrained by debt-to-equity covenant (>2:1).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Single-asset concentration risk; Inability to reset rents broadly due to long-term contracts; Debt covenant restrictions on buybacks; Strata ownership complexities at Nirlon House.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic on rentals; Defensive on expansion plans; Non-committal on special dividends but open to final dividend upside; Transparent on tax and accounting impacts.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The apparent spike in finance costs is an accounting artifact (Ind-AS discounting) rather than a cash burden; The Citi renewal rate (>INR 185) signals strong pricing power despite lack of broad market reset opportunities.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: NKP is the primary asset with ~100% occupancy; Nirlon House is a strata-owned building with complexities limiting redevelopment or significant updates; Citi renewal confirmed at significantly higher rates with annual escalations.

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margins robust at 77.93%; Finance cost appears high (9.7% implied) due to Ind-AS accounting on security deposits; Actual cash cost is 30-day T-bill + 233 bps (~7.7%).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth via contracted annual escalations; Margins stable at ~78% EBITDA; No new leasing inflows expected immediately due to 99.7% occupancy; Capex: None for expansion; Commissioning: N/A.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Leasing pipeline minimal; 25,000 sq ft renewed by Citi at >INR 185/sq ft; Only ~7,800 sq ft vacant across NKP and Nirlon House as of Dec 31, 2025.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Limited to rental escalations and occasional vacancy resets; No vertical expansion or multi-city plans currently; Redevelopment of NKP not on the immediate agenda.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Nirlon delivered steady 6% YoY income growth driven by contracted escalations and a significant rental reset on the Citi renewal (>INR 185/sq ft), while the shift to the new tax regime boosted PAT margins to 54%. With near-100% occupancy and INR 325 Cr cash, the key variable remains the final dividend or potential buyback, though debt covenants currently limit the latter.

open.item: Company's priority is to ensure timely servicing of its loans (HSBC Green Loan facility of Rs. 1,230 crore, outstanding Rs. 1,150 crore as on March 31, 2026, rated AA+/Stable by Crisil).
Company to continue reducing its carbon footprint by increasing the share of electrical power sourced from renewables and improving the efficiency of water consumption during FY2026-27.

Company's priority is to ensure new licensees are able to occupy and commence their operations as contracted, and to proactively pursue renewal of all other licenses due for renewal at competitive rates.
Company's priority is to ensure an efficient capital allocation strategy in order to maximize shareholder value.
Company's stated priority for FY2026-27 is to ensure timely servicing of its loans under the HSBC Green Loan facility.
Company's stated priority for FY2026-27 is to pursue an efficient capital allocation strategy in order to maximize shareholder value.

Board recommended a final dividend of Rs. 15 per share (@150%) for FY2025-26, in addition to the interim dividend of Rs. 15 per share (@150%) already paid, subject to Members' approval at the 67th AGM.

drhp.business: Nirlon Limited develops and manages Nirlon Knowledge Park (NKP), an approx. 23-acre Industrial Park/Information Technology Park in Goregaon (East), Mumbai, spanning five completed development phases with approx. 47.63 lakh sq. ft. of constructed area and approx. 30.8 lakh sq. ft. of licensable area. The Company earns license fee income by licensing this space to well-regarded, predominantly institutional occupants in the IT/ITeS, Banking and Financial Services (including GCC) sectors.

risks.note: Nearly all revenue derives from license fees on one property, Nirlon Knowledge Park (NKP) in Goregaon (East), Mumbai; there is no diversification across other buildings, cities or business lines, so occupancy, rate or catastrophe risk at NKP directly hits the whole Company.

The Company's Rs 1,230 crore HSBC Green Loan (Rs 1,150 crore outstanding as at March 31, 2026) is secured by a first and exclusive mortgage charge over NKP's land, buildings and structures - its sole income-generating asset.

Relatively inexpensive commercial real estate in suburbs beyond Borivali/Mulund and in satellite cities (Navi Mumbai) and other metros (Chennai, Pune, Hyderabad, Bangalore) could keep commercial license rates under pressure in NKP's micro-market.
risks.risk: Competitive rate pressure from cheaper suburban/satellite markets

risks.note: Management explicitly flags the impact of AI on employment generation in the GCC sector in India as a potential new risk, which could reduce incremental hiring and demand for commercial office space that NKP depends on.
Management explicitly flags the impact of extreme heat and climate change on the commercial office market generally and on NKP in particular as a risk to identify and monitor.
risks.risk: Climate change / extreme heat impact on the office market

risks.note: Geopolitics, US tariff/protectionist policy shifts and global conflicts (e.g., Middle East) are flagged as creating inflation, foreign-exchange volatility and recessionary pressure that weigh on real estate investment decisions in India, including Mumbai.

The Company had only 3 employees during FY2025-26, all Key Managerial Personnel (Executive Director & CEO, Company Secretary, CFO), so operations and property/lease management are dependent on a very small internal team and on outsourced/related-party service providers.
